0 Dou Dizhu Fight the Landlord (Dou Dizhu) is a climbing game said to have originated in Hubei province but is now popular all over China. In each hand one player, the 'landlord', plays alone and the others form a team. The landlord's aim is to be the first to play out all his cards in valid combinations, and the team wins if any one of them manages to play all their cards before the landlord. [Rating: 4/10] Felt like a much worse version of Big 2. Not much you can realistically do if opponents have bombs and you don't.

[Rating: 4/10] The bidding and two-on-one gameplay set this apart from other climbing games, but I'm not fond of the bombs.

[Rating: 5/10] From www.pagat.com:  "Fight the Landlord (Dou Di Zhu) is a climbing game primarily for three players, but also playable by four. In each hand one player, the "landlord", plays alone and the others form a team. The landlord's aim is to be the first to play out all his cards in valid combinations, and the team wins if any one of them manages to play all their cards before the landlord. The game is said to have originated in Hubei province but is now popular all over China, and is also extensively played on line."  Game Rated: #2855.

[Rating: 5/10] Another variation on Dourak/President. Has too many different possible combinations that can be played to remember for casual play.

[Rating: 5.5/10] Fun climbing game, but lacks the depth of Big Two. Due to the large number of combinations, it is a huge advantage to have the lead. Since the Landlord has the first lead, they usually win. Also, since bidding order is randomized, there is a good deal of luck.

[Rating: 6/10] 130930 Played on a plane from China. Good fun, as a 3P variable partnership game with bidding.
